meaning_by_symbol.drift: patterns are sliding across faces slowly, with edges blurred or smearing and a hum wavering in pitch and unsettled
meaning_by_symbol.layered: a hum with layered tones stacked
meaning_by_symbol.split: a hum split into two or more competing tones
meaning_by_symbol.hollow: a hollow-sounding hum or hollow sound when tapped, depending on context
meaning_by_symbol.N: new symptoms follow, with a short description or code after it
meaning_by_symbol.F2: double fail; the second-stage silent step also failed
meaning_by_symbol.trace: run a finger along all edges of the relevant face, and when used alone later, run a finger along each of the 4 edges that border the named face, one by one
meaning_by_symbol.1: ALIGN: faces flicker randomly light and dark with no pattern, the hum is broken and irregular and starts and stops randomly, and edges remain normal
meaning_by_symbol.2: DRIFT: patterns slide across each face slowly like colors drifting, edges are blurred or smearing, and the hum is wavering in pitch and unsettled
meaning_by_symbol.3: ECHO: the faces are too bright and almost hard to look at, the hum has layered tones stacked, and some faces show frozen patterns that do not respond to touch
meaning_by_symbol.4: LEAK: corners are dark, edges are faint, the center is okay, and the hum is hollow
meaning_by_symbol.5: LOW: all faces are dim and the hum is a whisper
meaning_by_symbol.6: HI: all faces are blazing bright, there is a buzzing hum, and there is heat
meaning_by_symbol.7: PHASE: opposite faces pulse bright and dark alternately, and the hum is two-tone
meaning_by_symbol.8: RESONANCE: one face is dramatically brighter than all others, there is intense localized vibration near that face, there is a high-pitched whine near that face, and the other faces look normal
meaning_by_symbol.9: corner lock: one or two corners are glowing bright, there is a clicking sound, and there is heat at those corners
meaning_by_symbol.10: BOUNDARY: edges wobble or flex when touched, faces look slightly curved or bulging so the box shape is distorted, and the hum sounds muffled like underwater
meaning_by_symbol.11: STALL: patterns are frozen and dim, the hum is silence, and the surface is cold
meaning_by_symbol.12: HARMONIC: the hum is split into two or more competing tones that clash, patterns alternate between two different configurations, and edges shimmer like two patterns fighting
meaning_by_symbol.13: THERMAL: it is very hot all over but dim, the hum is a low rumble rather than a tone, the surface feels rough or gritty, and the light has a reddish tint
meaning_by_symbol.14: VOID: faces glow normally but sound hollow when tapped, and there is a dark center when held to light

meaning_by_symbol.fanX+Y: fan at X then Y sequentially

reply.rationale: No segmentation survives the paradigm-evidence requirements. Many repeated strings are only surface resemblances (e.g. cl-, fa-, -er, -rm), and the numbered condition codes 1–14 are opaque aliases for whole named states rather than compositional number morphemes. The promising procedural forms with X/Y/N placeholders (cloth@X, bell×N@X, fanX+Y, brd@X,Ys,INT, etc.) do suggest a notation, but this codebook does not supply enough attested same-frame substitution among concrete fillers to justify a morpheme/class network under the required standards. In particular, X/Y/N/INT are metavariables, not observed fillers; proposed splits like bell + @X or fan + X would require classes whose members are not compositionally evidenced by multi-entry contrasts here. Because false morphology is worse than none, the defensible analysis is a flat lexicon.
